[b]Feb 10, 2025 Business:[/b]
The Thýren stock market officially closed with a 4% increase, a small increase compared to two days prior when it was formally announced that THEP would open offices in both Thýren and Hydronia, which saw a 12% increase in all major stocks. In other news, construction has begun on oil processing and refining plants with the government stating that they have a potential to be up within five to six months provided no delays, until then all crude oil imported through THEP will be held on unused container ships, with a monthly cap of 1200 barrels per month until the refineries are finished. Currently the famed Thýren watchmaker Dormaar and Doffen is considering opening regional offices in Hydronia by August 2025. This comes after the Crystal Casino's formally announced it was going to begin doing online business within Hydronia within the end of the month.

[b]Pùnapà and the Urûntù system[/b]
Starbound Roleplay.
[i]Lair of Pùnapà, the capital planet of Chimor, and as well the lair of the Thrynn race.[/i]
[b]Main Star-Urûntù[/b]
The orange-dwarf, Urûntù was seen as the most likely star to sustain life by Chimú scientists, at least, in a range of our ships.
[b]Sansákàn[/b]
The "burnt" is the first planet in Urûntù's orbit, a planet full of craters, extinct volcanoes, and extinct valleys all over it surface, any , molecule on it thin atmosfere is usually tear apart, due the long exposure to the Urûntù UV rays.
The thin atmosphere of the planet is composed of sulfur, hydrogen, and chlorine, while some other minor gases.
The surface, despite the chaotic attacks of UV from the star, have several Thrynn and Chimú outposts, mining copper, antimony and hydrogen.
[b]Pùnapà [/b]
The lair of Thrynn, a reptilian lizard-like specie, great allies of Chimor, which share their homeworld with us, great enginners, indeed, most of our ships are made by Thrynn hands, they were well integrated into our Empire, and as long we exchange metals, such as iron , silver and other conductive metals, they are willing to be our allies, when the Empire first arrived, the Thrynn were still colonizing Sansákàn for mining copper and Chìpantí, for aluminium, though the Chimor introduced the Thrynn to the silver, the best conductive metal, rare in their world, but common in Chimor, which made both people friendly and allies, until today, the Thrynn are our best ally of the empire, and longest dating race we are friendly with, since 2132.
 Pùnapà has one single moon, called Chillor(lesser Chilla/Moon), and the planet has a strong magnetic field to protect against it star, stronger than Erene, which for humans can cause some diziness and headache, but after generations, we somewhat adapted to the conditions and have many cities all over the planet's continents.
The Atmosphere is, in general, composed of nytrogen, Oxygen, and Carbonic gas and some lesser gas.
The resources includes, tin, zinc, iron, lead, silver in very small numbers, plutonium etc... silver being the most valuable.
[b]Guébiòn[/b]
Named after the Thrynn name for the planet, Gw'eehbio, the planet is a lifeless piece of rock, with a brown-yellowish surface, it has a heavy pressure and relatively thick atmospher, composed of Co2, while the surface is a violent active seismically place, the clouds are the only place where cities were made, by Chimú settlers around 2278, to extract CO2, and hydrogen.
The surface, which is very active in Guébiònquakes/Earthquakes, has nickel, tin, magnesium and titanium found it, deep in the planet is believed to have some water depots underground, with possibly Ammonia being also present.
[b]Bíllachê[/b]
Coming from the Thrynn "B'ihyaxe", this planet is "a tragedy", second the Thrynn,  it was once a thriving planet, with water and many resources on it, a good atmosphere composed of Nytrogen and oxygen,  and many metals on it surface, even the life was thriving there, but large amounts of methane gas were expanding fast, making the planet warmer and warmer, it was  soon reduced to some minor islands, while the temperature grows more and more every year, the life retreated to the deep sea.
Despite all this, explorers of Chimú landed on the planet at 2177, to study the greenhouse effects on the planet, and possibly revert them.
[b]Chìpantí[/b]
The winter planet is a cold planet, the last rocky planet of the system, is cold and covered in ice, and also lair of the Elowan, a race that dislikes the Thrynn, due living under them as slaves for a 2 centuries, the Elowan are a race with fur covering all their bodies, which are smaller and robust, similar to a biped small bear, their homeplanet, Chìpantí, which they call it El'eran, which is rich in chromium, copper, aluminium, and iron, which made the Thrynn enslave the Elowan to mine such metals, mostly needing to drill sheets and sheets in ice.
The planet has a very decent atmosphere, with Oxygen, nytrogen, and small amounts of greenhouse-effect gases, some small lakes and rivers that are not frozen can be found in the equator of the planet during summer.
The Chimor colonized this planet as many others, establishing outposts and cities, their relationship with the Elowan is neutral, with them preferring living in their ice caves rather involving with Chimús, though some Elowans showed great cunning for science, even some of the Empire's scientists in Chìpantí and Bíllachê are Elowans.
[nation]Shahzada[/nation] RP

[b]The Funeral | [sub][i]Garden of the Heroes, Stormhaven, Norrhollow [/i]| 11 February 2025[/b][/sub]

It's very simple Eske. Don't mess it up. One step forward. Use your right foot. Now your left. Right. Left. Right. Left. Follow the beating in your heart, or sing a little song and follow the beat there. Left. Right. Left. Oop, looks like you nearly tripped yourself. Should've kept on counting starting from the Right if I were you. But it's fine, you're fine, it's all probably still fine. Next time, I'll remember that you prefer starting with the left foot. Breathe in and out, you're running late now so you really should quit stalling.

Left. Right. Left. Keep walking, walking, walking. Did you remember your script? That tiny piece of paper you kept throwing away and rewriting all night? Because all that hard work will be for nothing if you decide to misplace it now. Check your pocket. It's still there, isn't it? But that's fine. Who knows what would happen if it suddenly disapeared. Left. Right. Left. Right. Left. You tripped a little bit again. You better hope that nobody saw that. Think of the papers, the gaffes, the headlines. Left. Right. Left. Is your script still in your pocket?

Check it again. It's there. It was always there. Why do you worry so much over such pointless little things, Eske. Check it again. Yes, it's still there. Honestly, it's more likely to fly away in the winds if you keep taking it out over and over again. Left. Right. Left. The lieutenant governor is smiling at you, Eske. Smile back. Smile back. Smile back. Smile back. Smile back.

That was a terrible smile, but whatever. She wasn't legitimately smiling at you either way. It's fine, you're fine, it's probably all fine.

You stand on the edge of the stairs and walk up. Left. Right. Left. Not too loud now, the stomps might freak out land commissioner Bastrup. Softly. Softly. Alright, you're at the wooden podium stand now. See the fine oak grain running down its fine structure? That could be you if you tried a little bit harder. Strand up straight. Not too straight. You'll look like a robot. Stand up straight damn it! There we go, all good. Check your notes. Check it again.

It's there, isn't it? Take it out. Left. Right. Left. What are you shifting around for? Everyone's looking at you. The lieutenant governor already introduced you. Imagine that: the audience had already given out everything about your bio, how much of a tough guy you are, on how you crackdown on the criminals that wreak havoc on the streets of Stormhollow. And that guy is now just standing in front of the podium, doing absolutely nothing? Get a grip. Check your script.

It's still there. Place it on the podium. No, it's crooked. Remove it. Place it on the podium. Fix it. Fix it. Fix it. All good? Well, not really, because it's been almost a minute of you just doing absolutely nothing. You're in front of everyone, Eske. Do something. Left. Right. Left. No, stop moving. Do something productive. Yes that's right, smile for the cameras, pretend that this was all just to build up suspense. Nevermind poor old Espedal lying in his coffin beside you, his ghost's probably waiting for you to start talking already. But it's fine, you're fine, it's all probably still fine. Because you're about to talk. Right?

Talk now. Look down at the script and remember the words. Look up and into their eyes to instill confidence. Talk now.

[list]"Last week, on a fine winter's night at Peterson's Bar, I was with Mr. Espedal together with a few friends. It was an informal night out among the boys after a hard day's work."[/list]

Good. That's good. Maybe a bit jittery, but you're doing well Eske. Except no, you aren't. The script said to introduce him as "Gunnar", not "Mr. Espedal". For Ada's sake, Eske, he's your friend. You've known him since college, and you're still introducing him with his last name? His wife's watching you Eske. She's down there in the galleries, looking at you. Your best friend's wife is looking at you, looking at the coffin, and she's probably wondering what the hell you're thinking introducing your own best friend without even bothering to give his real name. But it's fine, you're fine, it's all probably still fine. Just keep talking and it'll all be over soon.

You talk about how much you enjoyed that little moment in the Bar and how fickle life is that just a week after, he'd be there, laying in that coffin in that finely (maybe too finely) dressed suit and tie, his skin waxy and shiny from the gaudy embalming that Old Gunnar said was going to make him look really angelic when he goes. You talk about his impact on society. Talk over this faster. Everyone already knows Gunnar was a good guy. Come on Eske, you're delivering a eulogy, so at least try to make your friend sound look a cool guy and not just some random politician on corporate payroll. Talk. Talk. Talk. Yes I know you're basically skipping over your script, but who cares. Do you think the people care about your hard work? No, they don't. They care about making things interesting, so make it interest!

[list]"He was a good man, brimming over with the excellence of titans. His mind was deeper than the great ocean deep, which rather than dividing continents would bind the national spirit of this great nation together."[/list]

Good. Good. You ended up repeating the word "nation" technically, but it's fine, you're fine, it's all probably still fine. Oh what, I was just pointing it out. Stop pausing, stop stumbling, not every criticism is supposed to be analyzed, not while everyone's watching you. Talk. Talk. Talk. Look at your script. It's almost done, isn't it? Gunnar's soul is waiting to be released and you're holding him up. So finish it already. You go into more detail about his character. You shoot out a few prerehearsed jokes intended to follow up the basic build-up you've been concocting. A chortle here. A chuckle there. That's good. You're good.

You're doing great, you're doing swimmingly. Now finish it. Come on, compare and contrast Gunnar with the other guys and finish it.

[list]"Caas and Ipsen were the heroes of their time, men who fought for our nation in the greatest moment of strife. We are no longer in those days, and it is often said that in these tranquil days there will be weak men. But Gunnar was not weak. May we remember his great duties to Norrhollow and all of High Albany and enshrine his soul on the tomb that ensconces the heroes of old. Happy are we that have been endowed with his kindness through all these changing years."[/list]

A thunderous applause. Or rather, an applaused prepared by the House which everyone else decided to run along with. Smile for the camera, you did great. You're done now, and Gunnar is maybe proud. But you have to step down now, Eske. Left. Right. Left. That's good. Take the stairs, go down, away from the public view. Left. Right. Left. Uh oh, looks like someone's walking up to you.

[list]"Are you alright, Mr. Almstedt? You're breathing awfully hard..."[/list]

Oh. It's just the lieutenant governor. She's such a darling isn't she? To be worrying over you, you frustrating mess. Go ahead, give her a smile and say you're fine. Or do you honestly want to cause a scene at your friend's funeral? No? Then smile. That's it. No, not it. You're smiling too much. Great, now she's backing away. Was it because she realized you were fine? No, it's because she probably thought you were trying to kill her with that nasty smile. Stop smiling. Don't ever smile again. At least you're free of that interaction.

Sit down Eske, you're done for today. Let the others give their eulogies, finish the service, and let's take five. Now that wasn't so hard, was it?
